text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your new movement symptoms, can you describe exactly what movements you are experiencing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. Since you started risperidone two months ago, have you noticed any involuntary movements, such as stiffness, tremors, or restlessness, that were not present before?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: These symptoms of inner restlessness and the inability to remain still are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotic medications like risperidone. To confirm this diagnosis, I need to rule out other causes of agitation or movement disorders. REQUEST TEST: Neurological_Exam
